AI/LLM Observations - Aug. 2026

August 2026

In Response

A post from Thomas Fuchs went by on Mastodon asking for thoughts on the ethics of AI/LLMsterms. The topic has been bubbling in the back of my mind for a few weeks. While this post is a response, it's more a place to use writing to solidify my own thoughts.

Points for Feeling

I'm not at the point where trying to write a single, cohesive post makes sense. For now, it's bullet points. (We'll get to the ethical stuff at the end. I've got sort out how things feel first.)

  • I write a lot of code. My point of view is coming from the perspective of a developer.

  • I wonder how much variation folks have when they use the term "vibe coding". For me, it's when someone gives an LLM the ability to read and update their code directly.

    Something that still freaks me out. Getting into why that is is a topic for another day.

  • The reason for the clarification of the term is because if someone asks me if I use AI to code, the answer is yes. I use duck.ai to prompt in effectively the same way I use search engines. In fact, I'm increasingly going to it as the first move.

    I read the code it gives me, then place it into my codebase myself after thinking through what it's going to do and how it's going to do it. Updating my mental map of the process I'm working on.

    (That may be one of the biggest things that freaks me out about full on vibe coding. I don't feel like I'd have a mental map of what's going on if I'm not seeing everything myself)

  • I should point out that I start with documentation before going to either an AI/LLM or a search engine. Especially if I've got some prior knowledge about what I'm doing.

    For example, I'm working with rust's nom(https://docs.rs/nom/latest/nom/index.html) parsing library. While there's a lot to it, I've spent a lot of time with it. It's easy for me to find answers directly form the docs when I hit a sticking point.

  • I've learned a bunch from using LLMs like a search engine. The code samples they return are generally much larger than I get on Stack Overflowso. That larger surface area has frequently lead to second order learning where I'm exposed so something new that's adjacent to the thing I was looking form.

Ethicality

  • There's this thing in the good place where they talk about how much harder it is to get into heavan because of the complexity of the world.

Footnotes

terms I'm using the terms "AI" and "LLM" here interchangeably. There are some definitions that would differentiate between the two, but they mean the same thing here.
